title: Real Estate Wholesaling for Beginners with NO MONEY [Step By Step]
summary: A real-estate investor explains wholesaling for beginners: assigning purchase contracts for a fee, why earnest money and due diligence remove risk, and a direct-to-seller marketing and high-volume sales process, with pitches for his own education and data products.

assertions.quote: instead of actually having to go buy it from the seller he can sell this contract right here to a buyer

verdicts.note: Contract assignment is an established practice, though several states now require licensing or disclosure for it.

assertions.quote: you can make your earnest money deposit for as little as you want I've seen contracts where an earnest money deposit is ten dollars

verdicts.note: Deposits can be small, but finding discounted sellers requires paid data and marketing, and the pitch omits licensing and legal costs.
Deposits can be small, but finding discounted sellers takes paid data and marketing, and deposits are often at risk once contingencies lapse.

assertions.quote: finding the buyer is a lot easier than finding the seller of a great deal

verdicts.note: Cash-buyer demand for discounted property is deep; motivated-seller lead generation is the costly, competitive part.

assertions.quote: with direct marketing you're going direct to the seller so there's no other middleman therefore you're going to have bigger spreads

verdicts.note: Removing intermediaries raises the spread per deal, but marketing cost per closed deal is substantial and rising with competition.

assertions.quote: if we are the same skill level and I make twice as many calls as you I'm gonna get twice as many deals as you

verdicts.note: Volume raises deal count, but list quality and diminishing returns on the same leads make it sub-linear.

assertions.quote: if you back out on day 29 you get all your money back with no issues

verdicts.note: Standard contingency mechanics where sellers accept them; regulators object because sellers bear the cost of tied-up contracts.

assertions.quote: the average person that is actually closed takes seven touches that means you would have had to talk to them seven times

verdicts.note: Multi-touch conversion is a general sales finding; the specific count is folklore.

assertions.quote: it's just easier to get deals when you're sitting in the seller's living room

verdicts.note: In-person rapport plausibly improves negotiation, but it is self-reported practice without controlled comparison.
